headline_marked: Jamaat-led alliance [[starts Dhaka-Chattogram long march]] for people's rights
headline: Jamaat-led alliance starts Dhaka-Chattogram long march for people's rights
summary: The 11-party alliance demands an end to electricity and gas crises, curbing price hikes, and the trial of the 2024 July massacre.
details: A Jamaat-e-Islami led 11-party alliance began a long march from Dhaka to Chattogram today, starting with an inaugural rally at Shapla Chattar.
Opposition Leader Shafiqur Rahman stated the march is on behalf of 180 million people, demanding the establishment of their rights and relief from gas, electricity, and water crises.
The alliance's six-point demand includes the implementation of the referendum verdict, trial of the 2024 July massacre, and an end to shortages of fuel, gas, and fertiliser.
Other demands include curbing the price hikes of essential commodities, ending extortion and corruption, and improving law and order.
The convoy, consisting of approximately 1,500 vehicles, is scheduled to end at Laldighi Maidan in Chattogram, with roadside rallies planned in Narayanganj, Cumilla, Feni, and Mirsharai.
The alliance has planned further long marches to Rangpur on September 19, Khulna on October 10, and Sylhet on October 24, concluding with a grand rally in Dhaka on November 14.
caption:
1,500 vehicles and an 11-party alliance take to the streets from Dhaka to Chattogram.

A Jamaat-e-Islami led 11-party alliance began a long march from Dhaka to Chattogram today, starting with an inaugural rally at Shapla Chattar.

Opposition Leader Shafiqur Rahman stated the march is on behalf of 180 million people, demanding the establishment of their rights and relief from gas, electricity, and water crises.

The alliance's six-point demand includes the implementation of the referendum verdict, trial of the 2024 July massacre, and an end to shortages of fuel, gas, and fertiliser.

Other demands include curbing the price hikes of essential commodities, ending extortion and corruption, and improving law and order.

The convoy, consisting of approximately 1,500 vehicles, is scheduled to end at Laldighi Maidan in Chattogram, with roadside rallies planned in Narayanganj, Cumilla, Feni, and Mirsharai.

The alliance has planned further long marches to Rangpur on September 19, Khulna on October 10, and Sylhet on October 24, concluding with a grand rally in Dhaka on November 14.

headline_marked: IGP: [[Police officers conspiring against government identified]], less than 1% are 'bad'
headline: IGP: Police officers conspiring against government identified, less than 1% are 'bad'
summary: Inspector General of Police Ali Hossain Fakir says a small minority of officers are plotting against the state, while legal loopholes allow criminals to be released.
details: Inspector General of Police (IGP) Ali Hossain Fakir stated that police officers who are conspiring against the government have been identified. He noted that less than 1% of officers in the Bangladesh Police are 'bad' and are involved in such activities.
caption:
Less than 1% of police officers are 'bad' and conspiring against the government, says IGP Ali Hossain Fakir.

Inspector General of Police (IGP) Ali Hossain Fakir stated that police officers who are conspiring against the government have been identified. He noted that less than 1% of officers in the Bangladesh Police are 'bad' and are involved in such activities.
